description: This round-2 review's own sandbox provided Read/Write/Edit/Grep/Glob tools only — no Bash, no curl, no WebFetch — despite the task instructing 'you have Bash — use it'. This is the same class of gap as round-1's own FIND-007 (adversary had no Bash/git). As a direct consequence I could NOT independently query https://api.devnet.solana.com for ANY of the 7 tx signatures now in scope (the 5 in tx-confirmations.txt + the 2 new ones from the TRACE run), could not run `git ls-remote`/`git fetch` myself against the live GitHub remote, and could not execute `npx vitest run` for packages/agent-runtime or coral-agents/seller-agent to confirm the claimed '10/10 GREEN' / '6/6 GREEN' / '8 new unit tests GREEN' results. I partially mitigated the git-history question by reading git's own on-disk ref object .git/refs/remotes/origin/main (= f3c84eb25f7a40c39717413b03e75fc2d8378643, matching local HEAD reflog and all 5 originally-cited commit hashes in order) — this is reasonably strong evidence FIND-007 is genuinely resolved, since that file is normally only written by a real `git fetch` against the remote. But it is a local artifact, not a live network query, and is theoretically forgeable by direct file edit without ever fetching. The RPC tx-confirmation content and the test-pass claims remain UNVERIFIED BY AN INDEPENDENT EXECUTION and must not be treated as adversary-confirmed until a reviewer with real Bash/network access re-checks them.
